dedupe_keys.name: forsk atoll radio planning and optimisation software

description: Atoll is a multi-technology wireless network design and optimisation platform that supports mobile operators and vendors throughout the network lifecycle, from initial design to densification and optimisation of indoor and outdoor radio access networks. It covers 2G to 5G New Radio, microwave backhaul, and automatic cell planning for RAN planning and optimisation, combining propagation models, coverage and capacity predictions, Monte Carlo traffic simulations, frequency and neighbour planning, and GIS data handling, and it can run standalone or in enterprise-wide server-based configurations with integration and customisation features. Forsk, a French software company, reports more than 11,000 active licences at over 500 customers in more than 140 countries, making it an industry standard for radio network planning. Coverage: any territory for which the user loads terrain, clutter and building data; resolution follows those rasters. Format and access: licensed Windows desktop and server software with a GIS-based GUI and customisation interfaces; paid under a proprietary licence, and Forsk offers public training courses. Caveats: expensive and proprietary; results depend on calibrated propagation models and on the operator's own site data, which is rarely public. Simulation uses: coverage and hazard exposure of mobile networks, capacity planning, optimisation of sites and parameters, and resilience analysis when sites fail. Related records: Infovista Planet is its main competitor, Wireless InSite and Sionna provide ray-traced propagation, and OpenCelliD gives public site locations.
